name: Keep README Updated
description: Update README when adding features, changing setup, or modifying environment requirements.
content:
# Keep README Updated Rules

- Update the README whenever you add a new feature that users or developers need to know about
- Keep setup instructions current — if you add a new environment variable, dependency, or build step, update the README
- Include a "Getting Started" section with copy-paste-ready commands — `git clone`, `npm install`, `npm run dev`
- Document all environment variables with descriptions and example values — use `.env.example` and reference it
- List prerequisites (Node.js version, Python version, Docker, etc.) at the top of the setup section
- Keep the project description accurate — update it when the project's scope or purpose changes
- Document available scripts/commands — `npm run test`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` with descriptions
- Include a project structure overview for repositories with non-obvious organization
- Remove outdated information — deprecated features, old API endpoints, removed environment variables
- Use badges for build status, test coverage, and version — but only if they're maintained and accurate
- Add a "Contributing" section if the project accepts contributions — link to contribution guidelines
- Review the README during each release — treat it as part of the release checklist
